question: For a 2026 research artifact on unlinkable agent commerce and machine payments, produce a deep survey covering four areas: (1) Network-layer anonymity systems for low-latency confidential broadcast and metadata privacy: DC-nets (Dissent, Verdict, Atom, Riffle, ZIPNet, Flashbots Network-Anonymized Mempools Flashnet), mixnets (Loopix, Nym, Mixminion), HOPR, and how they compare on bandwidth, latency, anonymity-set size, and threat model. (2) Anonymous credential schemes that carry spendable state: Anonymous Credit Tokens (ACT) in Privacy Pass WG, Rate-Limit-Nullifier (RLN) based ZK credit schemes including Vitalik Buterin and Davide Crapis Feb 2026 ZK API Usage Credits proposal, Brave Boomerang, batched Privacy Pass, Coconut credentials. Status, deployments, tradeoffs. (3) Agent commerce protocols and their identity defaults: Coinbase x402, Stripe Tempo Machine Payments Protocol MPP, ERC-8004 Trustless Agents, MCP, Google A2A, Google Mastercard AP2. Where each defaults to attributed identity vs anonymous. (4) Agentic search and AI inference as workloads: what makes them suitable for query-atomic unlinkable payment, who is building agentic search in 2026, how the workload profile differs from traditional payment use cases. Today is May 14 2026.
synthesis:
# Deep Survey of Unlinkable Agent Commerce and Machine Payments (2026)

## 1. Network-Layer Anonymity Systems
**Note:** This section is not covered in the current synthesis. For a complete survey, further research is needed on DC-nets (Dissent, Verdict, Atom, Riffle, ZIPNet, Flashbots Network-Anonymized Mempools Flashnet), mixnets (Loopix, Nym, Mixminion), HOPR, and their comparative performance on bandwidth, latency, anonymity-set size, and threat model.

---

## 2. Anonymous Credential Schemes with Spendable State

### Comparative Table (2026)

| Scheme / Protocol                | Core Mechanism & Spendable State | Deployment Status (2026) | Tradeoffs / Limitations | Key Sources |
|----------------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|------------------------|-------------|
| **Anonymous Credit Tokens (ACT)** | Keyed-verification anonymous credentials (KVAC); BBS-style signatures; tokens carry integer balance, support partial spending, unlinkable redemptions, and cryptographic nullifiers for double-spend prevention. | IETF CFRG draft (Aug 2025); Cloudflare research demo live; integration with Privacy Pass being explored. No evidence of large-scale production deployment, but active prototyping and standards work. | Strong unlinkability, partial spending, and balance privacy; issuer cannot link issuance to spend; cryptographic nullifiers prevent double-spend. Protocol is new—ecosystem and interoperability still maturing. | [IETF draft](https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-schlesinger-cfrg-act-00.html), [Cloudflare demo](https://act-issuer.research.cloudflare.com/) |
| **RLN-based ZK Credit Schemes** | Rate-Limiting Nullifier (RLN) using ZK proofs; users prove quota compliance without revealing identity/history; nullifiers prevent double-spend; can support decrementable/spendable state (e.g., API usage credits). | Deployed in Status Network (Ethereum L2, gasless spam prevention); open-source RLN modules (vacp2p/zerokit) used in Waku and other P2P protocols; Vitalik Buterin & Davide Crapis's 2026 ZK API Usage Credits proposal is an evolution of this model. | Strong privacy and unlinkability; scalable to millions of users (Sparse Merkle Trees); proof generation can be slow for complex circuits; trusted setup required for some ZK systems; circuit complexity is nontrivial. | [Status blog](https://status.app/blog/zero-knowledge-proof-zk-privacy-status), [Status nullifier explainer](https://status.network/blog/what-is-a-nullifier-zero-knowledge-cryptography), [vacp2p/zerokit](https://github.com/vacp2p/zerokit) |
| **Brave Boomerang** | Decentralized privacy-preserving incentive protocol; builds on Black-Box Accumulator/Wallets and Privacy Pass; tokens represent ad interactions, stored and updated on client, with ZK proofs for reward computation; supports spendable state (reward points). | Production deployment in Brave Rewards (browser-based ad incentives); Boomerang protocol live as of 2024; privacy pass-based token issuance and redemption for premium services. | Strong privacy (no user identity revealed to issuer or advertisers); decentralized reward computation; relies on client-side storage and ZK proofs; integration with L1 blockchains for public reward verification. | [Brave Boomerang blog](https://brave.com/blog/boomerang-protocol/), [Brave premium privacy doc](https://github.com/brave/brave-core/blob/master/docs/premium_account_privacy.md) |
| **Batched Privacy Pass** | Blind signature tokens (VOPRF-based); tokens issued in batches, redeemed one at a time; server cannot link issuance to redemption; supports time-limited and single-use tokens (spendable state via batch size and time windows). | Widely deployed by Cloudflare, Brave, and others for anti-abuse, premium access, and rate-limiting; standardized as RFC 9576 (June 2024); used in production for both anonymous access and paid services. | Strong unlinkability; simple client/server integration; batch issuance enables spendable state but no partial spending (tokens are atomic); server tracks spent tokens to prevent double-spend. | [RFC 9576](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9576.html), [Brave premium privacy doc](https://github.com/brave/brave-core/blob/master/docs/premium_account_privacy.md) |
| **Coconut Credentials** | Threshold selective disclosure credentials; support for re-randomization, public/private attributes, and unlinkable selective attribute revelations. No native support for decrementable/spendable state as of 2026. | No evidence of spendable/decrementable Coconut credentials or deployments as of 2026; only foundational research and selective disclosure applications. | Strong threshold issuance and selective disclosure; not suitable for spendable credit or decrementable state without major extensions. | [arXiv:1802.07344](https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.07344) |

#### Summary of Tradeoffs
- **ACT**: Most flexible spendable state (partial spending, anonymous change), strong unlinkability, but still in early adoption.
- **RLN-based schemes**: Deployed for rate-limiting/quota, strong privacy, scalable, but computationally intensive for complex circuits.
- **Brave Boomerang**: Practical, decentralized, privacy-preserving rewards with spendable state, but relies on client-side storage and ZK proofs.
- **Batched Privacy Pass**: Widely deployed, simple, but spendable state is coarse-grained (batch size/time window), no partial spending.
- **Coconut**: Focused on selective disclosure, not spendable state.

---

## 3. Agent Commerce Protocols and Identity Defaults

| Protocol / Standard                | Default Identity Model      | Rationale for Default                                                                                                    | Source(s)                                                                                              |
|-------------------------------------|----------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| **Coinbase x402**                   | Anonymous (by default)     | Designed for per-request, accountless payments; the payment receipt is the credential. Enables agent privacy and minimal onboarding friction. | [WorkOS blog](https://workos.com/blog/x402-vs-stripe-mpp-how-to-choose-payment-infrastructure-for-ai-agents-and-mcp-tools-in-2026), [Eco guide](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14839400-what-is-agentic-commerce-the-2026-guide) |
| **Stripe Tempo MPP**                | Attributed (session-based) | Session-based payments linked to Stripe’s compliance stack; attributed identity required for regulatory and fraud reasons. | [Stripe docs](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/mpp), [Tempo docs](https://docs.tempo.xyz/learn/tempo/machine-payments), [WorkOS blog](https://workos.com/blog/x402-vs-stripe-mpp-how-to-choose-payment-infrastructure-for-ai-agents-and-mcp-tools-in-2026) |
| **ERC-8004 Trustless Agents**       | UNKNOWN                    | No direct documentation or industry adoption evidence found as of 2026.                                    | UNKNOWN                                                                                               |
| **MCP (Model Context Protocol)**    | Attributed (by default)    | Used for agent-to-tool discovery; most deployments require attributed credentials for auditability and trust. | [Eco guide](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14839400-what-is-agentic-commerce-the-2026-guide)      |
| **Google A2A**                      | Attributed (delegated)     | Used for agent-to-agent delegation; attributed identity ensures accountability and secure delegation. | [Eco guide](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14839400-what-is-agentic-commerce-the-2026-guide)      |
| **Google Mastercard AP2**           | Attributed (mandate-based) | Uses cryptographic mandates (signed receipts) for regulatory compliance and non-repudiation. | [Eco guide](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14839400-what-is-agentic-commerce-the-2026-guide)      |
| **Visa TAP (Trusted Agent Protocol)**| Attributed (signed identity)| Signs agent identity into HTTP headers for merchant-side trust and fraud prevention. | [Eco guide](https://eco.com/support/en/articles/14839400-what-is-agentic-commerce-the-2026-guide)      |

**Summary:**  
- **Anonymous by default:** x402, for agent autonomy and privacy in micropayments, especially on crypto rails.
- **Attributed by default:** Stripe MPP, MCP, A2A, AP2, TAP—driven by compliance, fraud prevention, and auditability.

---

## 4. Agentic Search and AI Inference as Workloads

### Implementation and Suitability for Query-Atomic Unlinkable Payments

- **Agentic search and AI inference** are now handled by autonomous agents using LLMs and agent frameworks, with open standards like MCP enabling “Agentic Payments” [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/industries/agentic-payments-the-next-evolution-in-the-payments-value-chain/).
- **Protocols like BitGPT’s 402Pay** allow agents to embed signed micropayments into each API/inference request, achieving atomic, machine-to-machine payments at web scale [Decrypt/BitGPT](https://decrypt.co/317316/introducing-402pay-bitgpts-native-http-402-payment-stack-for-the-autonomous-ai-economy).
- **Decentralized solutions** (e.g., Wagmi Payments Protocol) facilitate direct, on-chain transactions between AI agents [Wagmi](https://gptonline.ai/nevermined/).

#### Why These Workloads Suit Query-Atomic Unlinkable Payments
- **Atomicity:** Each query pairs with a deterministic payment; compute is delivered only if payment is received.
- **Privacy/Unlinkability:** Protocols minimize data leakage and transaction linkability, supporting pseudonymous commerce.
- **Automation:** AI agents dynamically authorize and settle payments without human intervention, ideal for high-frequency, low-value, privacy-sensitive workloads [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments).

### Leading Builders and Protocols

| Builder/Protocol     | Description & Role                                                                                       | Source |
|----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| BitGPT / 402Pay      | HTTP 402 payment stack for AI agents; atomic, privacy-preserving microtransactions for inference/API. | [Decrypt/BitGPT](https://decrypt.co/317316/introducing-402pay-bitgpts-native-http-402-payment-stack-for-the-autonomous-ai-economy) |
| Wagmi Payments       | Decentralized, web3-native protocol for AI-to-AI payments. | [Wagmi](https://gptonline.ai/nevermined/) |
| Visa (Trusted Agent Protocol) | Agentic payments with production deployments (Microsoft, Shopify, Stripe, Coinbase). | [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |
| Mastercard (Agent Pay) | Digital tokenization and orchestration for agentic payments. | [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |
| PayPal (Agentic AI Toolkit) | APIs for agentic payments, integrated with Perplexity and ChatGPT. | [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |
| Coinbase x402        | On-chain agentic payment protocol, high transaction volume.    | [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |

### Differences from Traditional Payment Use Cases

| Aspect                  | Agentic Search/Inference Payments      | Traditional Payments                   | Source |
|-------------------------|----------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|--------|
| Transaction Size        | Micro (fractions of a cent)            | Macro (dollars or more)                | [Decrypt/BitGPT](https://decrypt.co/317316/introducing-402pay-bitgpts-native-http-402-payment-stack-for-the-autonomous-ai-economy) |
| Frequency               | High (per query/inference)             | Low (per purchase/subscription)        | [Decrypt/BitGPT](https://decrypt.co/317316/introducing-402pay-bitgpts-native-http-402-payment-stack-for-the-autonomous-ai-economy), [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |
| Initiator               | Autonomous AI agent                    | Human user                             | [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |
| Atomicity               | Payment and service in one operation   | Payment and service often decoupled    | [Decrypt/BitGPT](https://decrypt.co/317316/introducing-402pay-bitgpts-native-http-402-payment-stack-for-the-autonomous-ai-economy) |
| Privacy/Unlinkability   | Often pseudonymous or unlinkable       | Typically traceable, KYC’d             | [Wagmi](https://gptonline.ai/nevermined/), [Decrypt/BitGPT](https://decrypt.co/317316/introducing-402pay-bitgpts-native-http-402-payment-stack-for-the-autonomous-ai-economy) |
| Approval Flow           | Dynamic, rules-based, continuous       | Manual, event-triggered                | [ARKM](https://info.arkm.com/research/what-are-agentic-payments) |

---

## Conclusion

Unlinkable agent commerce and machine payments in 2026 are driven by advances in anonymous credential schemes (ACT, RLN, Boomerang, Privacy Pass), a spectrum of agent commerce protocols (from anonymous x402 to attributed Stripe MPP/AP2/TAP), and the emergence of agentic search/AI inference workloads that demand atomic, privacy-preserving, high-frequency microtransactions. The field is rapidly evolving, with both web3-native and traditional payment giants adapting their infrastructure for the autonomous AI economy. A full survey should also include a comparative analysis of network-layer anonymity systems, which remains an open area for further research.
